issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem 7 (label linrob), the author bounds the L^2 norm of m(t) by C ||u_{\theta_0+h}(t) - u_{\theta_0}(t)||_{L^2}^2. By Taylor's formula, the pointwise remainder satisfies |m(t,x)| <= (1/2) ||f''||_\infty |u_{\theta_0+h}(t,x) - u_{\theta_0}(t,x)|^2. Taking the L^2 norm gives ||m(t)||_{L^2} <= (1/2) ||f''||_\infty ||u_{\theta_0+h}(t) - u_{\theta_0}(t)||_{L^4}^2, which is the squared L^4 norm, not the squared L^2 norm. On a bounded domain \Omega, ||w||_{L^4}^2 cannot be bounded by C ||w||_{L^2}^2, even under an H^{\bar \gamma} bound: for concentrated bump functions h_\varepsilon of width \varepsilon, ||h_\varepsilon||_{L^4}^2 / ||h_\varepsilon||_{L^2}^2 \asymp \varepsilon^{-d/2} \to \infty. In particular, at t = 0, ||m(0)||_{L^2} \sim ||h^2||_{L^2} = ||h||_{L^4}^2 cannot be bounded by O(||h||_{L^2}^2), rendering the claimed quadratic L^2 bound mathematically unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pure L^2 bound with a Sobolev interpolation bound: since h \in U(\bar \gamma, B) with \bar \gamma > d/2, use Gagliardo-Nirenberg / Sobolev interpolation to bound ||w||_{L^4}^2 \lesssim ||w||_{L^2}^{2 - d/(2\bar \gamma)} ||w||_{H^{\bar \gamma}}^{d/(2\bar \gamma)} \lesssim ||h||_{L^2}^{2 - d/(2\bar \gamma)}. Then adjust Condition 2 C to allow a power 1 + \delta (with \delta = 1 - d/(2\bar \gamma) > 0) and re-optimize the threshold condition on the prior smoothness parameter \gamma in Theorems 2, 5, and 1 to ensure that N \tilde \delta_N^{2+\delta} = o(1).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 7 fails as stated and proved. Consequently, Condition 2 C is not verified as claimed in Theorem 5 (label bvminv), and the quadratic linearization error estimate used in the proof of Theorem 1 (label ganzwien) becomes unestablished as written.
issues.title: Invalid L2 estimate for the nonlinear remainder in the linearization of the forward map
issues.why_classification: The issue invalidates the exact quadratic estimate in Theorem 7 and Condition 2 C, but it can be resolved without changing the overall proof architecture by bounding the L^4 norm via interpolation and slightly adjusting the regularity parameter \gamma to absorb the subquadratic exponent.
